transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-03-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Maya, Liam, Priya (Redwood) / Sara, Tom, Evan, Nina (Elmwood)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Goal: walk through Redwood model catalog decision criteria and intake for benchmarking open models; align on success metrics and deployment constraints (VPC/private, data residency, SSO).
- Outcome: agreed to pilot 8 candidate models, Redwood to provide bench runbook and sample CSV, Elmwood to return prioritized prompt set and SLOs.

Topics: decision criteria, compatibility matrix, bench selection, infra constraints (VPC, KMS), latency vs cost tradeoffs, rollout path (hosted -> dedicated -> private)

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick off real quick. i'm maya, i'm the AE on this account, with liam our se and priya on solutions. can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Sara (Elmwood): yes loud and clear, thanks.
[00:10] Tom (Elmwood): morning all, excited to see the practical side of the catalog, we've been digging through your docs a bit.
[00:18] Liam (Redwood SE): great. quick agenda - 1) decision criteria & scoring matrix, 2) how we pick bench candidates from the open-model catalog, 3) integration & deployment constraints, 4) next steps and pilot scope. we'll show a couple screenshots in the console.
[00:34] Priya (Redwood): heads up, some of the model names in the UI are abbreviations and sometimes auto-transcripts mixed kernels, so we'll call out exact hashes/versions in the runbook link.
[00:45] Evan (Elmwood Infra): important for us - we need clarity on private deployment options. we run HIPAA-adjacent workloads in some verticals and KMS + audit logs are must-haves.
[00:55] Nina (Elmwood Security): and SSO, SAML; we need to know how tokens are scoped and retained.
[01:05] Maya: totally. we'll cover redwood private and k8s on-prem options, plus our KMS integrations. quick poll - is latency SLO or cost the primary driver?
[01:14] Tom: SLOs first, cost second. 95th pct latency under 150ms for short chat completions.
[01:22] Sara: and quality on product recs needs to be top-tier - don't want hallucinations for item prices.
[01:29] Liam: good, we'll treat quality as accuracy metric in benching. our decision matrix has weighted columns: quality/accuracy (40%), latency (25%), cost (20%), ops complexity (15%). we can tweak weights.
[01:45] Speaker 5: mm-hmm
[01:50] Liam: here's the pragmatic picklist flow - from the catalog we export candidate models, run quick float and 8-bit quant benches, then select top 3 for production proof. note: quantization sometimes changes output quirks — we flag regen tests.
[02:10] Sara: can you explain the compatibility matrix? we had trouble mapping your "compat" column to our GPU types.
[02:18] Priya: sure, the matrix rows are models, columns are hardware families (A100, H100, L4, graviton inferentia-ish). compatibility is "runnable" vs "optimized" vs "verified". some of the older open models are runnable but not optimized and will hit higher token latencies.
[02:40] Evan: do you auto-select kernels or do we supply custom kernels? we have a constrained infra team.
[02:46] Liam: runtime does kernel selection automatically; but for private we can ship precompiled kernels if you want. also, our console shows a kernel map per model.
[02:56] Tom: what's the expected perf delta between hosted and private for the same model?
[03:02] Liam: depends heavily on network and instance type — hosted has caching, autoscaling, and prefix-KV cache enabled; private on-prem might be within 10-30% slower unless you use the same GPU family and kernel tuning.
[03:18] Maya: quick note - for benches we recommend using our 'throughput-basic' script, we share it in the runbook link.
[03:25] Sara: ok the team will need that.
[03:27] [04:01] Liam: showing console now - top-left is the catalog filter, you can filter by license (open/closed), tokenization profile, seq length, and compatibility. i run a filter for open models that have "verified for generation" tag. this narrows to about 25 candidates.
[04:20] Liam: we then run a pre-bench suite: latency single-stream, throughput steady-state, and qualitative regen tests. we also run a small eval set for elmwood prompts.
[04:32] Tom: how do you handle tokenizer mismatch? we sometimes use proprietary tokenizers and get different token counts.
[04:40] Priya: we normalize by measuring tokens per prompt using the model's tokenizer and include token inflation in cost estimates. we also show effective cost per useful token in the console.
[04:53] Nina: security question — where are bench logs stored and for how long?
[04:58] Maya: bench logs by default are in the customer's workspace for 30 days, but for enterprise private we can forward to your SIEM or store in your S3 and set retention. all bench runs have audit entries.
[05:12] Sara: good.
[05:15] Liam: walkthrough of compatibility matrix - note the 'fallback path' column: if primary model not available we route to a cheaper variant, e.g. 8-bit quant or smaller architecture. that helps maintain availability during spikes.
[05:32] Tom: curious about accuracy regressions after quant — you flagged this earlier. what's your guardrail?
[05:38] Liam: we run prompt-regression tests and quality delta thresholds; if quantization increases error beyond 2% we mark it as not recommend for that workload. also we store golden outputs for regen.
[05:52] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[05:56] Priya: another practical tip - for catalog picks we capture a "selection rationale" note in the UI so downstream SREs know why model chosen.
[06:05] Sara: nice. we'd like that - handoff is a pain for us.
[06:09] Maya: okay, moving to bench intake logistics - we propose a 3-stage intake: 1) intake survey (you fill in prompts, SLOs, traffic profile, allowed licenses), 2) smoke bench (fast runs on 8 candidates), 3) deep bench (top 3).
[06:26] Tom: timeframe?
[06:28] Maya: smoke bench ~ 3 business days after we get prompts + traffic sample; deep bench another 5-7 days. total pilot about 3 weeks.
[06:36] Evan: we need to run smoke bench in our VPC. is that possible?
[06:41] Liam: yes, we can run the bench harness pointing at your private endpoint; we can also provide an execution agent you run in your cluster to collect metrics and push back.
[06:52] Nina: and encryption in transit?
[06:54] Liam: TLS and mTLS support for agent connections, KMS integration for keys.
[06:59] Sara: okay cool.
[07:02] [07:40] Maya: let's talk model license constraints - some open licenses disallow commercial use or require attribution, we'll help with a license flag in the CSV. you'll have to sign off on any models with restrictive terms.
[07:55] Tom: we prefer permissive ones; we can't ship models with very restrictive clauses.
[07:59] Liam: note in console we mark license type (MIT-like, Apache-like, restrictive).
[08:06] Sara: can the bench pipeline include a human-in-the-loop quality check? we have domain-specific edge-cases.
[08:12] Priya: yes, we can add a small human eval stage or integrate with your internal annotators. we also support a labeled eval set upload.
[08:20] Evan: cost modeling — will you show units and expected $/1M tokens for each model?
[08:26] Liam: yes the optimize module computes effective cost per response factoring token counts and batching. we show idle GPU costs for dedicated pools too.
[08:34] Tom: how do you suggest we weigh cost vs quality? any standard thresholds?
[08:39] Maya: we typically recommend a Pareto frontier approach — present candidates on a 2D plot quality vs cost, pick knee points. for Elmwood's SLOs you may accept slightly higher cost for top accuracy for product recs.
[08:53] Sara: what about adaptive routing if we have mixed traffic?
[08:57] Liam: smart routing is supported - you can route high-value requests to higher-accuracy models and low-value to cheaper variants. routing rules can be tag-based per route.
[09:07] Speaker 7: (crosstalk)
[09:10] Maya: quick demo snippet - i posted a link in the chat to the bench runbook and to a sample CSV with model list and weights.
[09:18] Sara: got it.
[09:20] [10:00] Liam: caveat - some model names in open model ecosystems are duplicated; we always anchor by model hash and exact tokenizer id, please use those in the runbook.
[10:10] Tom: are there rate limits in dedicated mode? we need predictable throughput.
[10:16] Liam: dedicated gives predictable throughput based on reserved GPU count, autoscaling policies can add burst capacity, and we surface quotas in console. SLA guaranteed p99 latencies for reserved capacities are part of dedicated contracts.
[10:30] Evan: procurement question - do you support bring-your-own-license for models?
[10:34] Maya: if you have a vendor contract, yes we can integrate that into the catalog and mark it as BYOL.
[10:40] Nina: security audit - do you provide SOC2 reports and third-party pen-test artifacts?
[10:44] Maya: yes SOC2 type II, plus we can provide pen test attestations under NDA.
[10:50] Sara: ok great.
[10:53] [11:20] Priya: slightly switching context — example of a selection rationale we've used: for cold-start product recs we picked a mid-sized Llama-variant that had top regen scores and under 120ms single-shot latency after kernel tuning. cost was higher but acceptable because per-user LTV justified it.
[11:38] Tom: good to see concrete example.
[11:42] Liam: also note we instrument token-level traces so you can see per-token latency breakdown. that helped another retail customer reduce tail latency by moving to a different kernel.
[11:55] Sara: will you help with A/B rollout? we need to slowly migrate traffic.
[11:59] Maya: yes, rollout policies include canary %, automatic rollback on quality regressions, and multi-variant A/B testing baked in.
[12:09] Evan: what telemetry is shipped to our monitoring? can we push traces to datadog?
[12:14] Liam: we have integrations for datadog, prometheus, and you can forward logs to your S3.
[12:22] Nina: compliance question - data residency for EU customers?
[12:26] Maya: we support regional hosting and private control planes so your data stays in region; for private deployments you fully control residency.
[12:34] [13:05] Sara: thanks. quick practical ask - can you help prioritize the candidate set? we have internal bias toward some model families.
[13:11] Maya: yes, here's our recommended approach: we take your prompt set, sample token distribution, run smoke bench on 8 varied candidates (some larger/accurate, some cheaper), then compute weighted score using the matrix I mentioned. we'll return a ranked CSV with notes.
[13:29] Tom: what's in the ranked CSV?
[13:31] Liam: model id, tokenizer id, license, single-stream latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, quality score on your eval, notes on quant sensitivity, recommended deployment path.
[13:42] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[13:45] Priya: we'll annotate if a model is "risk: hallucination" from regen tests for your recs domain.
[13:52] Maya: ok we're approaching last 15 mins - let's call out explicit next steps and owners.
[13:57] Tom: yes please.
[14:00] Maya: action items - maya will send bench runbook + sample CSV; liam will prepare the throughput script and sample kernels; evan will send traffic profile and allowed IP ranges; sara will prioritize top 10 prompts and SLO doc. any additions?
[14:18] Evan: we'll also surface procurement timeline - we prefer to have pricing and pilot contract by 3/25.
[14:24] Maya: noted.
[14:26] Nina: security will need the SOC2 docs and to review pen-test artifacts, we'll set a separate call for that.
[14:33] Maya: great, i'll share links and a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.
[14:38] [15:00] Closing notes: agreed pilot scope: smoke bench 8 models -> pick top 3 -> deep bench -> canary rollout plan. target pilot completion ~ 3/31 if artifacts delivered on time.
[15:12] Tom: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[15:16] Sara: thanks all.
[15:20] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up in chat with links and a short checklist.

End of transcript.
